top.title: Arsenal goalkeeper Raya absent from training session
top.description: alkeeper David Raya was absent from Arsenal’s open training session on Monday ahead of their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund after he was forced off during the Gunners’ 2-2 draw at Newcastle. Understudies Kepa Arrizabalaga and Frenchman Illan Meslier took part in the workout as the players were put through their paces ahead of Tuesday’s home match against the Bundesliga side. Raya was replaced by Arrizabalaga in the 70th minute at St James’ Park on Saturday after an apparently innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula. The 31-year-old left the pitch clutching his left arm in visible discomfort with an apparent shoulder problem. Raya played a key role as Arsenal ended a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season and had started this campaign with seven clean sheets in 10 matches before the match in Newcastle. Raya’s injury came on the day Arsenal welcomed back William Saliba to the matchday squad. The France defender, who was an unused substitute, has not played this season because of an injury. Winger Bukayo Saka, who has been absent since October 21 due to a thigh injury, is still weeks away from a return. Arsenal have a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League table and have enjoyed a strong start to the league phase of the Champions League. top.title: Guenther Steiner warns George Russell: Do not "poke the bear" Max Verstappen
top.description: Motorsport photo Former Haas Formula 1 team principal Guenther Steiner has urged Mercedes driver George Russell not to "poke the bear" with Max Verstappen , after their war of words at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Russell hit out at Verstappen after the pair clashed in final practice, saying the Red Bull driver walks around "like they're bigger and better than everyone else" and that "somebody's got to stand up to that guy". The pair then swapped the lead repeatedly during the race on the Las Vegas Strip, until the Briton locked up and hit the wall on lap 48 while trying to pass team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second. Verstappen won, and afterwards said Russell was "so far below my level" . Speaking on The Red Flags Podcast , Steiner said he did not mind the two drivers disliking each other, but questioned why Russell had chosen to take Verstappen on. "No, I mean, I haven't got a problem with it, because in the end, if they don't like each other, what do I care?" Steiner said. "This has been going on for a long time between them, and obviously, George coming out to say, 'Oh, this guy behaves very arrogantly', or whatever he said about Max, and 'Somebody needs to stand up to him.' Yeah, good luck with that one, buddy. You see how that worked out." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes The former team chief said he respected Russell as a driver, but felt he had underestimated Verstappen's mental strength. "I respect George as a race car driver, but in the end, Max is just mentally superior. On how to manage mental things, he's so superior to you, do not poke the bear, in my opinion," he said. "There is no need for it, because you don't do yourself any favours. Get over it. Try to win races instead of picking a battle with the best driver out there, the strongest mental guy out there, because guess what? You're going to lose. "It's like there's nobody sitting down with him and saying, 'George, sometimes less is more. Just say nothing, do your own job,'" Steiner said, adding that the Mercedes driver should focus on winning races. "And then when you have got something to say because you beat the guy, pick your battle then. But as I said, if you cannot beat them, join them, and in the moment just shut up and get on with it." Verstappen's win moved him further clear in second place in the drivers' standings on 304 points. Russell, who finished ninth, is fourth on 264, behind Lewis Hamilton . top.title: Nonbinary athletes sue Philadelphia Marathon over unequal treatment in race categories
top.description: Three nonbinary runners sued Philadelphia and its marathon race director Tuesday over a rule that requires athletes to register as male or female to compete in the elite fields at the city’s marathon and half marathon. Winter Parts, Reed Williams and Miche Palmer, who use they/them pronouns, are asking a judge to order race organizers to end what the runners say is discrimination under the city’s Fair Practices Ordinance. They filed the suit against the city and race director Kathleen Titus in Philadelphia’s Court of Common Pleas, The Philadelphia Inquirer reported . At the Philadelphia Marathon on Sunday, runners could register as nonbinary in the open division, where they started in corrals behind the elite field. The difference extends to the finish line. When Williams won the nonbinary open division in 2024, they received $4,000. The men’s and women’s elite winners each earned $10,000, according to the lawsuit. “The hope is that this will be equal across the board in the future,” Parts told Philadelphia ABC affiliate WPVI . The city told the station it does not comment on pending litigation. Related : These trans and nonbinary candidates just made history Other local races already offer what the runners are seeking. The Philadelphia Distance Run offers an elite nonbinary category with equal prize money. The Independence Blue Cross Broad Street Run added one this year. Parts won it. The runners filed a complaint with the Philadelphia Commission on Human Relations in 2025. This year, the commission issued a right-to-sue notice, clearing the way for the runners to take their case to court. By the time the runners filed the complaint, local LGBTQ+ running groups had been pressing the city for a change for two years. Josh Fernandez, a nonbinary runner who was then executive director of Philadelphia-based Queer Run, told the Philadelphia Gay News in 2025 that city officials pointed to the sport’s governing body when advocates asked them to add an elite nonbinary category. “The governing bodies don’t manage the prize money. That’s managed by the people who manage the race, and the race is owned by the City of Philadelphia,” Fernandez said, adding that a third category would leave the men’s and women’s prizes intact. top.title: Karson Milbrandt’s 29% Strikeout Rate Sparks Rule-5 Buzz
top.description: Credit USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect During the 2026 Double-A season, Karson Milbrandt fanned close to 40% of batters he encountered. This dominant performance earned him a spot as the No. 70 prospect in Just Baseball’s August Top 100 update. Yet the Miami Marlins left him unprotected on the 40-man roster when the deadline passed on Tuesday. This move signals a major risk for a pitcher whose numbers looked unstoppable just months ago. A Tale of Two Seasons Milbrandt’s season splits tell a story of rapid rise and sudden fall. In Double-A this year, his strikeout-minus-walk rate soared to 29.0% from a solid 16.7% in 2025. He relied on a fastball that averaged between 18 and 20 inches of induced vertical break in A-ball during the 2025 season, according to Just Baseball . That same pitch lost its life once he reached the highest minor league level. Per Just Baseball, his vertical break fell to just 16 inches in Triple-A last season. The loss of movement made his fastball easier to hit, even though the speed remained high. His control issues grew worse as the competition got tougher. Milbrandt could not stay in the zone with his off-speed pitches, which led to a spike in walks. His earned run average climbed from a microscopic 1.34 in Double-A to a disastrous 8.39 across 64.1 innings in Triple-A. The team that drafts him in the Rule-5 Draft will need to figure out why his stuff vanished so quickly. The Pitcher Heavy Draft The upcoming Rule-5 Draft is expected to be dominated by pitchers again. Since 2022, pitchers accounted for 44 of the 53 MLB phase selections. Front offices operated under the assumption that a lockout might cancel the draft entirely. This fear left many desirable names like Milbrandt vulnerable to being taken by another team. If the draft happens, the list of seven intriguing names from Just Baseball could see a massive shakeup. Teams will look to grab high-upside arms that got left behind due to roster crunches. Other pitchers on the watch list include Zach Franklin of the New York Mets. Franklin is viewed as a true reliever prospect who was part of a trade return. The lack of protection for these arms suggests teams are betting on their potential over their current results. According to Just Baseball analysis, a team is guaranteed to take a flier on Milbrandt. The real question remains about what went wrong and how to fix it. Looking Beyond the Marlins The situation in Miami highlights a broader trend in how teams handle young arms. The Marlins have a deep system, but they could not protect everyone before the deadline. This leaves fans wondering if they lost a future star or just exposed a flawed pitch. The data shows a clear drop in spin and command that needs immediate attention. If a new team can restore his vertical approach angle, his value could skyrocket. top.title: ‘That’s just wrong’: Draymond Green reacts to what people said right after Steph Curry’s injury
top.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images The Golden State Warriors have finally won a game. Steve Kerr’s men went on an eight-game winning streak after their terrible start to the season, but they then lost each of their next five games. On Sunday, the Warriors returned to winning ways, beating the Celtics 88-87. One of the big reasons behind Golden State’s problems is the absence of Steph Curry, who has been out for a while now due to injury. Yaxel Lendeborg was tasked with replacing the Warriors’ talisman, but that expectation from people was just wrong, says Draymond Green. Draymond Green hits back at people expecting Yaxel Lendeborg to replace Steph Curry Lendeborg had such a good start to his NBA career when he was playing with Curry. The 24-year-old looked like a real force, and he was many people’s pick to win the Rookie of the Year award when he was firing on all cylinders. That form convinced many people that he could do a job for the Warriors no matter the circumstances, which is why some expected him to just fill Curry’s shoes after his injury. Lendeborg then went through a really rough run, which affected him. Green has now claimed that people should’ve never put him in that position. He said, as per Luca Evans on X : “First off is understanding that no one’s gonna be Steph. No one’s gonna slide into that role and all of a sudden become the greatest shooter to ever live, the greatest point guard to ever live, or a top-five player to ever live. That’s a tough role to slide into. “And so I think initially, as – with Steph going out, Yax, you can see him answering the questions like, ‘Yeah, I need to do this.’ And everybody’s like, ‘You know what, our second option, you need to slide in.’ And that’s just wrong. “And I’ve been here for 15 years – no one can replace Steph Curry. 15 years from now, no one will replace Steph Curry. He is one of one. “And so, then, it’s about, what do we need to do? And the reality is, come out and use each other. Use each other to create advantages.” Green is spot on. Expecting a rookie like Lendeborg, despite his incredible talent and potential, to seamlessly fill Curry’s shoes is absolutely absurd. Nobody can do that. The Warriors had to change their style to find a way to win without their main man, and they did that well against the Celtics. That is exactly what they need to keep doing until Curry is back in action. top.title: Tennessee fined $250,000 after fans took Josh Heupel’s golf ball suggestion against Lane Kiffin
top.description: Lane Kiffin’s second return to Neyland Stadium as a visiting head coach produced the same scene as his first, and on Sunday it produced the same response from the Southeastern Conference. With 3:14 left in No. 9 Tennessee’s 27-13 win over LSU on Saturday, play stopped after a pass interference call as fans in the student section sent golf balls and mustard bottles toward the LSU bench. Tigers players moved toward midfield to get out of range until the field was cleared. Tennessee Vols head coach Josh Heupel has been named in The Athletics rankings of the top 25 coaches in college football. Photo Credit: Tennessee Athletics The league fined Tennessee $250,000 under its sportsmanship, game management and alcohol availability policies. That is the same amount, under the same policies, the SEC assessed in October 2021, when Kiffin brought Ole Miss to Knoxville and was hit by a golf ball during a 20-minute delay. As it did five years ago, the conference left alcohol sales in place and reserved the right to suspend them later. Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel set the tone for the rematch in July, when he was asked at SEC Media Days in Tampa about Kiffin’s first trip back to Knoxville as LSU’s coach. “Certainly hope our fanbase hasn’t cooled off, whether it’s the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard or our sports stores making sure they’ve got reinforcements on the golf balls. Hopefully, Knoxville is ready for his arrival,” Heupel said . He called the remark a joke on the SEC coaches teleconference during game week. “That was a tongue-in-cheek comment at SEC Media Days. But we need our fans to be a part of this football game and create a tough environment on Saturday afternoon. I have no questions that our fans will be there early, will be hydrated and will be ready to compete for 60 minutes, too,” Heupel said. Why Kiffin was not surprised by the golf balls “Probably not when the coach says that at SEC Media Days, to go buy your golf balls. And I’m not being critical of him. I’m laughing at it. But they listened to their coach. So no, that doesn’t surprise me,” Kiffin said after the game. Sunday’s fine is Tennessee’s second fan-conduct penalty of the season. The SEC hit the school for $500,000 after fans stormed the field following an Oct. 17 win over then-No. 6 Alabama, money that went to the Crimson Tide under league policy. A week later, South Carolina owed the same amount for storming its own field after beating Tennessee, which effectively sent that half-million back to Knoxville. top.title: Marc Marquez: 'Curbing my instincts was key to winning 2026 MotoGP title'
top.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez says his 10th world championship title took more of a mental effort than any of his others. Marquez overturned a yawning 102-point deficit after an early-season injury absence to grab the crown in last weekend's Portuguese Grand Prix, with one round remaining. Riding with fitness limitations following his surgery in May, there were several weekends on which Marc was the not the fastest rider. But his ability to limit the damage in unfavourable situations and maximise points when he had an advantage proved decisive. Key to that strategy was avoiding mistakes - which in turn required the Spaniard to curb his racer's instinct to always go for victory. As Marquez explained after the race at Portimao, this was a psychological skill he developed during the course of 2026. "You know, this was the one [championship] that I worked more [the most] on my mental side. Because it was the only way. "I already understood that in the first part of the season, [my] instinct was not working anymore. "Always I want to win. You know, I'm a fighter, but I didn't feel that I must win, yes or yes. Because if you have that mentality in this championship, it was impossible to win. "This new Marc Marquez, new mentality, gives me the chance to finish races in seventh place,[or] fifth and take points. And yeah, of course, then at good circuits you need to win." Brad Binder, Red Bull KTM Factory Racing, Marco Bezzecchi, Aprilia Racing, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team He expanded on the theme at the subsequent press conference dedicated to his triumph. Asked if this was the title for which he had to show the most resilience and the toughest mentality, Marc agreed. "Yes. For that reason, I said [in the pre-event press conference last Thursday] this is the best [version of] Marc. Because the best athlete, I believe that arrives [an athlete reaches his best] when you can control yourself and when you can control your mental side. "And this year, I just worked on my mental side, because I understood that my physical condition was arriving one point [had hit a ceiling]. "And then I said, 'OK, give up, try to train in a normal way, try to, of course, do extra work with the physiotherapist, but work in a normal way.' "'What do I need? Braking, hauling the bike, and that's it. And try to be very fit.' "But especially, [I needed] to understand where it was possible and where it was not possible. And this was the main point." That approach worked almost to perfection following his surgery. Until the sprint race in Portugal, when he fell almost within sight of the flag. "Since I came back, I never crashed in a sprint or main race. Yesterday, yes - but it was a big warning." Marquez took that warning to heart on Sunday, riding even more carefully to bag an eighth place that was enough to become 2026 MotoGP champion. top.title: ‘Disgusting football’: Robert Saleh does not hold back on ’embarrassing’ Titans loss
top.description: Tennessee Titans Coach Robert Saleh talks with the media after the joint practice with the Seattle Seahawks at Vanderbilt Health Football Center Friday, Aug. 21, 2026. The Tennessee Titans’ defense got absolutely shredded by the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, as Dallas scored touchdowns on each of its first six drives on the way to a 51-30 win. It was the third straight game in which the Titans allowed at least 40 points. After the game, head coach Robert Saleh didn’t hold back. Saleh called his team’s defensive performance “disgusting” and “embarrassing,” adding that the blame for it “starts with me.” Titans’ Rough First Season Under Saleh Saleh’s first season in Tennessee has been a difficult one. The Titans opened the year with five straight losses, prompting the team’s CEO to issue an apology to fans . Tennessee finally got in the win column with a 26-20 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6. But the Titans haven’t won since, dropping to 1-9 with Sunday’s loss. The defense has been a big part of the problem. Tennessee allowed 43 points in an overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and 40 points in a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars before Sunday’s game in Dallas. According to ESPN, the Titans are now just the fourth team since the 1970 merger to allow 40 or more points in three consecutive games, joining the 1975 Cleveland Browns, the 1981 Baltimore Colts, and the 2004 Titans. ‘Disgusting football’ On Sunday, the Cowboys racked up 480 yards of total offense. Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards, and CeeDee Lamb had 132 receiving yards. Dallas scored on every drive except the last one, when it simply kneeled out the clock. It was a disastrous performance from the Titans, and when Saleh was asked what needs to change on defense after the loss, he gave a blunt answer. “There’s a lot of things that need to change. Obviously, it’s disgusting football. It’s embarrassing football. And obviously, that starts with me,” Saleh said, via the Titans . Saleh was then asked how he can call a game when nothing is working. “That’s why I get paid. I got to figure it out,” Saleh said. He also made it clear how he wants his players to feel about the performance. “I want to — hopefully, they feel pissed. Just feeling something,” Saleh said. When asked what part of the defense needs fixing the most, Saleh pointed to his players losing their individual matchups. “When I go back and watch this tape, I have a feeling I’m going to know exactly what it is. The NFL is a game of one-on-ones, and when you get a one-on-one, you’ve got to win your opportunities. And today, they won their opportunities, and we didn’t,” Saleh said. We’ll have to see how the team bounces back from this, but it’s pretty clear that Saleh was not impressed by the showing. In a public health advisory, the Academy said the World Health Organisation (WHO) had classified PJ.2.1 as a “Variant Under Monitoring”, although its current assessment indicates a low additional global public health risk. nigeria.title: Abia Police condemn officers over pregnant woman’s hospital ordeal
nigeria.description: By Steve Oko The Abia State Police Command has condemned the conduct of some of its personnel who allegedly stopped a man conveying his pregnant wife to hospital over the absence of a displayed vehicle number plate. The incident, captured in a viral video that has generated reactions on social media, involved officers attached to the Surveillance Patrol and Guard Team of Ubakala Divisional Police Station. The man was reportedly taking his pregnant wife to hospital after she began experiencing labour contractions when he encountered the officers, who allegedly insisted on taking him to the police station for driving without a displayed registration number plate. Reacting to the incident, the Police Command said it had identified the officers involved and commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the encounter and determine their level of responsibility. In a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, the Command acknowledged that the man was driving without a displayed number plate, contrary to road traffic regulations. It explained that vehicle identification was important, particularly in view of prevailing security challenges, including vehicle theft and the use of unidentified vehicles for criminal activities. The Command, however, said enforcement of traffic regulations should be guided by sound judgment and consideration for human welfare, especially in emergency situations. On the claim that the man’s wife was in labour, the police said preliminary information indicated that she was fine and had not given birth as of the time of the statement. It added that no medical evidence had been presented to substantiate the claim that she was about to deliver. Despite this, the Command expressed displeasure over what it described as the officers’ apparent failure to demonstrate sufficient empathy towards the pregnant woman. The outgoing Commissioner of Police, AIG Wilfred Olutokunbo Afolabi, reiterated that the police had a statutory responsibility not only to prevent and detect crime and maintain law and order but also to protect lives, uphold citizens’ rights and assist people in distress. He stressed that police duties must be discharged with professionalism, empathy, restraint and respect for human dignity. According to him, although the Command would continue to enforce the law, such responsibilities must be carried out with humanity and consideration for prevailing circumstances. The Command assured members of the public that the investigation would be thorough and that appropriate disciplinary measures would be taken if misconduct was established. nigeria.description: Sekinat Osundiji Presidential spokesman Daniel Bwala has said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) is not worried about the opposition ahead of the 2027 general election, insisting that its political rivals are not prepared for the contest. Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, stated this during an interview on Channels Television, where he dismissed suggestions that the ruling party was apprehensive about the growing activities of opposition parties. He said the APC was confident about its political standing, adding that the opposition was not ready for the election. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” Bwala said. His comments followed questions about President Tinubu’s decision to expand his campaign itinerary beyond the initial 12 states, amid reports of attacks on campaign materials and the president’s convoy. Defending the adjustment, Bwala described it as a strategic decision rather than an indication that the APC was worried about its political opponents. “President Tinubu is not scared. It is a matter of strategy. He is a chess player, who studies the moves of his opponents before deciding on his next move,” he said. He, however, acknowledged that the ruling party was working to secure voters’ support, saying it would be wrong to assume that Nigerians had already decided to re-elect the president. “We are not worried, but we are working hard because we respect the will of the people. We cannot take their votes for granted,” Bwala said. On the political situation in the North, Bwala described the region as a major battleground in the 2027 election, noting that the president’s campaign activities there were part of a deliberate strategy. He rejected suggestions that the North was united against Tinubu, arguing that the position of individual political leaders should not be interpreted as the collective position of the region. “There is no unanimous adoption of a candidate by any bloc in Nigeria, not even in the North. The position of one political leader should not be taken as the position of the entire region,” he said. Bwala also argued that the president had made significant efforts in the South-West, which informed his decision to concentrate more campaign activities in other regions. nigeria.description: By Steve Oko, Regional Editor, South-East Former Senate President and Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Board of Trustees, Senator Adolphus Wabara, has backed moves by opposition parties to present a consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections, urging political leaders to sacrifice personal ambitions in the interest of rescuing Nigeria. Wabara said opposition unity had become imperative in view of the country’s political and economic challenges, insisting that national survival, democratic stability and the welfare of Nigerians should take precedence over individual presidential ambitions. The former Senate President, who spoke exclusively with Vanguard, urged opposition presidential hopefuls to rise above personal interests, ego and political calculations and rally behind a credible candidate capable of challenging the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). He said the moment demanded political courage, compromise and patriotism, warning that failure by opposition leaders to unite could weaken the country’s democratic space and prolong the hardship facing citizens. His position comes amid ongoing consultations among opposition parties, including the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Allied People’s Movement (APM) and Social Democratic Party (SDP), to forge a common front ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The parties are expected to deepen discussions at a proposed opposition summit scheduled for November 30, where the question of a consensus presidential candidate and a broader framework for political collaboration are expected to feature prominently. Wabara argued that the opposition’s strength lay not in the number of presidential candidates contesting against one another but in its ability to unite behind one candidate with the political capacity, national reach and popular support to challenge the APC. He warned that allowing multiple opposition candidates to divide the votes of Nigerians seeking change could give the ruling party an electoral advantage without a meaningful challenge. According to him, the overriding objective should be to rescue Nigeria from the control of a few political interests while millions of citizens grapple with economic hardship, insecurity, unemployment and declining living standards. Describing the country’s situation as a threat to democracy, Wabara called on opposition leaders to demonstrate statesmanship by supporting whoever emerges as the consensus candidate, even if doing so requires them to shelve their presidential ambitions. nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army, working alongside other security agencies, have cleared additional sections of a suspected Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) and Eastern Security Network (ESN) camp in Imo State, uncovering and neutralising improvised explosive devices (IEDs). The operation, conducted on November 21 around Awomama in Oru East Local Government Area, was part of ongoing security offensives launched on November 16 and 17, according to the Army. The joint operation involved troops of the 34 Artillery Brigade and personnel of the Nigerian Navy, Nigerian Air Force, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS) and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC). Security sources said the joint team advanced into the Tango 2 and Tango 3 sections of the suspected camp at about 6:30 a.m., where they discovered that the locations had been heavily fortified with explosives. With the support of Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) personnel, the troops located and successfully neutralised the improvised explosive devices. The operation also led to the recovery of two battery components suspected to have been used to trigger the explosives. The clearance operation is part of sustained efforts by security agencies to dismantle suspected criminal hideouts and prevent attacks in the area. nigeria.title: PANDEF mourns Bayelsa boat accident victims, urges coastal roads
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has mourned victims of the boat accident around Oweikorogha Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which reportedly claimed several lives, including youths and children. The socio-political organisation also renewed its call on the Federal Government and governments of oil-producing states to prioritise the construction of roads and bridges to connect isolated coastal communities and reduce their dependence on water transportation. PANDEF, in a statement signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, said it received the news of the accident, which occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, with shock and sadness. The organisation described the incident as heartbreaking and commiserated with the affected families, the Bayelsa State Government, residents of Southern Ijaw and the affected communities. It said the tragedy reinforced its longstanding position that inadequate road infrastructure had left many coastal communities with limited transportation options, making water travel a necessity for their residents. According to PANDEF, the Federal Government should, as an interim measure, support state governments in acquiring adequate seaworthy vessels to meet the transportation needs of coastal communities. The organisation also called on emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work with the Bayelsa State Government to provide assistance to survivors and bereaved families. It urged the relevant authorities to strengthen enforcement of water transportation safety regulations, including compliance with passenger safety protocols, the use of appropriate safety equipment and the operation of vessels that meet prescribed seaworthiness standards. PANDEF said measures must be taken to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies, stressing the need for improved transportation infrastructure and stricter safety standards across the coastal areas. The statement read in part: “While mourning this tragic loss, PANDEF calls on the relevant emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work closely with the Bayelsa State Government to ensure that all necessary measures are taken to assuage the impact on survivors and bereaved families. “More importantly, [they should] take all necessary measures to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies.” The organisation expressed solidarity with the victims’ families and the people of Bayelsa State, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased and comfort for those affected by the tragedy. nigeria.description: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the UK is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades. Bulldozers have been digging up the ground for the vast £800-million ($1 billion) Havant Thicket project near the southern coastal port of Portsmouth. Like much of Europe, Britain endured record-breaking heat this summer and, despite the return of rains as the country moves into winter, parts are still grappling with drought conditions. “We’ve got increasing problems with our water security in the UK,” climate scientist Hannah Cloke from Reading University told AFP. “We need to really think about how we’re storing that water because this problem is only going to get worse.” Scientists have warned extreme weather events are likely to become more frequent and more intense as the global climate changes. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP By mid-November, almost all of England remained in drought, with some areas classified as suffering severe drought, according to the Environment Agency. Potentially exacerbating matters, existing reservoirs were only 60 percent full, 19 percentage points below the seasonal average. For policymakers, the situation poses a longer-term challenge as the thirst for water increases with a rising population and the growth of heavy water-using industries such as data centres. Under England’s National Framework for Water Resources published in 2025, the country could face a daily water supply shortfall of five billion litres (1.3 billion gallons) by 2055, with resources under pressure. At the sprawling Havant Thicket site, Portsmouth Water chief executive Bob Taylor said the industry was waking up to the scale of the challenge after successive droughts and hot summers. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP The issue, he stressed, was not necessarily how much rain falls over the course of a year, but when it falls. Winters are becoming wetter, while summers are increasingly dry. “Without reservoirs you can’t store that intense rainfall and put it somewhere where it can be used at another time,” Taylor said. The new reservoir will eventually hold up to 8.7 billion litres of water, helping secure supplies for hundreds of thousands of people. Fed in part by winter surpluses from a major spring already tapped by Portsmouth Water, it has become one of the flagship projects in a broader shift in Britain’s water strategy. The government has approved the construction of nine major reservoirs by 2050, and last year relaxed planning rules to speed up projects after decades of under-investment in water infrastructure. Together, the future reservoirs could deliver an additional 670 million litres of water per day. ‘

You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. sports.title: Guenther Steiner warns George Russell: Do not "poke the bear" Max Verstappen
sports.description: Motorsport photo Former Haas Formula 1 team principal Guenther Steiner has urged Mercedes driver George Russell not to "poke the bear" with Max Verstappen , after their war of words at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Russell hit out at Verstappen after the pair clashed in final practice, saying the Red Bull driver walks around "like they're bigger and better than everyone else" and that "somebody's got to stand up to that guy". The pair then swapped the lead repeatedly during the race on the Las Vegas Strip, until the Briton locked up and hit the wall on lap 48 while trying to pass team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second. Verstappen won, and afterwards said Russell was "so far below my level" . Speaking on The Red Flags Podcast , Steiner said he did not mind the two drivers disliking each other, but questioned why Russell had chosen to take Verstappen on. "No, I mean, I haven't got a problem with it, because in the end, if they don't like each other, what do I care?" Steiner said. "This has been going on for a long time between them, and obviously, George coming out to say, 'Oh, this guy behaves very arrogantly', or whatever he said about Max, and 'Somebody needs to stand up to him.' Yeah, good luck with that one, buddy. You see how that worked out." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes The former team chief said he respected Russell as a driver, but felt he had underestimated Verstappen's mental strength. "I respect George as a race car driver, but in the end, Max is just mentally superior. On how to manage mental things, he's so superior to you, do not poke the bear, in my opinion," he said. "There is no need for it, because you don't do yourself any favours. Get over it. Try to win races instead of picking a battle with the best driver out there, the strongest mental guy out there, because guess what? You're going to lose. "It's like there's nobody sitting down with him and saying, 'George, sometimes less is more. Just say nothing, do your own job,'" Steiner said, adding that the Mercedes driver should focus on winning races. "And then when you have got something to say because you beat the guy, pick your battle then. But as I said, if you cannot beat them, join them, and in the moment just shut up and get on with it." Verstappen's win moved him further clear in second place in the drivers' standings on 304 points. Russell, who finished ninth, is fourth on 264, behind Lewis Hamilton . sports.description: Three nonbinary runners sued Philadelphia and its marathon race director Tuesday over a rule that requires athletes to register as male or female to compete in the elite fields at the city’s marathon and half marathon. Winter Parts, Reed Williams and Miche Palmer, who use they/them pronouns, are asking a judge to order race organizers to end what the runners say is discrimination under the city’s Fair Practices Ordinance. They filed the suit against the city and race director Kathleen Titus in Philadelphia’s Court of Common Pleas, The Philadelphia Inquirer reported . At the Philadelphia Marathon on Sunday, runners could register as nonbinary in the open division, where they started in corrals behind the elite field. The difference extends to the finish line. sports.description: Credit USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect During the 2026 Double-A season, Karson Milbrandt fanned close to 40% of batters he encountered. This dominant performance earned him a spot as the No. 70 prospect in Just Baseball’s August Top 100 update. Yet the Miami Marlins left him unprotected on the 40-man roster when the deadline passed on Tuesday. This move signals a major risk for a pitcher whose numbers looked unstoppable just months ago. A Tale of Two Seasons Milbrandt’s season splits tell a story of rapid rise and sudden fall. In Double-A this year, his strikeout-minus-walk rate soared to 29.0% from a solid 16.7% in 2025. He relied on a fastball that averaged between 18 and 20 inches of induced vertical break in A-ball during the 2025 season, according to Just Baseball . That same pitch lost its life once he reached the highest minor league level. Per Just Baseball, his vertical break fell to just 16 inches in Triple-A last season. The loss of movement made his fastball easier to hit, even though the speed remained high. His control issues grew worse as the competition got tougher. Milbrandt could not stay in the zone with his off-speed pitches, which led to a spike in walks. His earned run average climbed from a microscopic 1.34 in Double-A to a disastrous 8.39 across 64.1 innings in Triple-A. The team that drafts him in the Rule-5 Draft will need to figure out why his stuff vanished so quickly. The Pitcher Heavy Draft The upcoming Rule-5 Draft is expected to be dominated by pitchers again. Since 2022, pitchers accounted for 44 of the 53 MLB phase selections. Front offices operated under the assumption that a lockout might cancel the draft entirely. This fear left many desirable names like Milbrandt vulnerable to being taken by another team. Other pitchers on the watch list include Zach Franklin of the New York Mets. Franklin is viewed as a true reliever prospect who was part of a trade return. The lack of protection for these arms suggests teams are betting on their potential over their current results. According to Just Baseball analysis, a team is guaranteed to take a flier on Milbrandt. The real question remains about what went wrong and how to fix it. Looking Beyond the Marlins The situation in Miami highlights a broader trend in how teams handle young arms. The Marlins have a deep system, but they could not protect everyone before the deadline. This leaves fans wondering if they lost a future star or just exposed a flawed pitch. sports.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images The Golden State Warriors have finally won a game. Steve Kerr’s men went on an eight-game winning streak after their terrible start to the season, but they then lost each of their next five games. On Sunday, the Warriors returned to winning ways, beating the Celtics 88-87. One of the big reasons behind Golden State’s problems is the absence of Steph Curry, who has been out for a while now due to injury. Yaxel Lendeborg was tasked with replacing the Warriors’ talisman, but that expectation from people was just wrong, says Draymond Green. Draymond Green hits back at people expecting Yaxel Lendeborg to replace Steph Curry Lendeborg had such a good start to his NBA career when he was playing with Curry. The 24-year-old looked like a real force, and he was many people’s pick to win the Rookie of the Year award when he was firing on all cylinders. That form convinced many people that he could do a job for the Warriors no matter the circumstances, which is why some expected him to just fill Curry’s shoes after his injury. Lendeborg then went through a really rough run, which affected him. Green has now claimed that people should’ve never put him in that position. He said, as per Luca Evans on X : “First off is understanding that no one’s gonna be Steph. No one’s gonna slide into that role and all of a sudden become the greatest shooter to ever live, the greatest point guard to ever live, or a top-five player to ever live. That’s a tough role to slide into. “And so I think initially, as – with Steph going out, Yax, you can see him answering the questions like, ‘Yeah, I need to do this.’ And everybody’s like, ‘You know what, our second option, you need to slide in.’ And that’s just wrong. “And I’ve been here for 15 years – no one can replace Steph Curry. 15 years from now, no one will replace Steph Curry. He is one of one. “And so, then, it’s about, what do we need to do? And the reality is, come out and use each other. Use each other to create advantages.” Green is spot on. Expecting a rookie like Lendeborg, despite his incredible talent and potential, to seamlessly fill Curry’s shoes is absolutely absurd. Nobody can do that. The Warriors had to change their style to find a way to win without their main man, and they did that well against the Celtics. That is exactly what they need to keep doing until Curry is back in action. sports.title: Marc Marquez: 'Curbing my instincts was key to winning 2026 MotoGP title'
sports.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez says his 10th world championship title took more of a mental effort than any of his others. Marquez overturned a yawning 102-point deficit after an early-season injury absence to grab the crown in last weekend's Portuguese Grand Prix, with one round remaining. Riding with fitness limitations following his surgery in May, there were several weekends on which Marc was the not the fastest rider. But his ability to limit the damage in unfavourable situations and maximise points when he had an advantage proved decisive. Key to that strategy was avoiding mistakes - which in turn required the Spaniard to curb his racer's instinct to always go for victory. As Marquez explained after the race at Portimao, this was a psychological skill he developed during the course of 2026. "You know, this was the one [championship] that I worked more [the most] on my mental side. Because it was the only way. "I already understood that in the first part of the season, [my] instinct was not working anymore. "Always I want to win. You know, I'm a fighter, but I didn't feel that I must win, yes or yes. Because if you have that mentality in this championship, it was impossible to win. "This new Marc Marquez, new mentality, gives me the chance to finish races in seventh place,[or] fifth and take points. And yeah, of course, then at good circuits you need to win." Brad Binder, Red Bull KTM Factory Racing, Marco Bezzecchi, Aprilia Racing, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team He expanded on the theme at the subsequent press conference dedicated to his triumph. Asked if this was the title for which he had to show the most resilience and the toughest mentality, Marc agreed. "Yes. For that reason, I said [in the pre-event press conference last Thursday] this is the best [version of] Marc. Because the best athlete, I believe that arrives [an athlete reaches his best] when you can control yourself and when you can control your mental side. "And this year, I just worked on my mental side, because I understood that my physical condition was arriving one point [had hit a ceiling]. "And then I said, 'OK, give up, try to train in a normal way, try to, of course, do extra work with the physiotherapist, but work in a normal way.' "'What do I need? Braking, hauling the bike, and that's it. And try to be very fit.' "But especially, [I needed] to understand where it was possible and where it was not possible. And this was the main point." That approach worked almost to perfection following his surgery. Until the sprint race in Portugal, when he fell almost within sight of the flag. "Since I came back, I never crashed in a sprint or main race. Yesterday, yes - but it was a big warning." Marquez took that warning to heart on Sunday, riding even more carefully to bag an eighth place that was enough to become 2026 MotoGP champion. sports.title: ‘Disgusting football’: Robert Saleh does not hold back on ’embarrassing’ Titans loss
sports.description: Tennessee Titans Coach Robert Saleh talks with the media after the joint practice with the Seattle Seahawks at Vanderbilt Health Football Center Friday, Aug. 21, 2026. The Tennessee Titans’ defense got absolutely shredded by the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, as Dallas scored touchdowns on each of its first six drives on the way to a 51-30 win. It was the third straight game in which the Titans allowed at least 40 points. After the game, head coach Robert Saleh didn’t hold back. Saleh called his team’s defensive performance “disgusting” and “embarrassing,” adding that the blame for it “starts with me.” Titans’ Rough First Season Under Saleh Saleh’s first season in Tennessee has been a difficult one. The Titans opened the year with five straight losses, prompting the team’s CEO to issue an apology to fans . Tennessee finally got in the win column with a 26-20 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6. But the Titans haven’t won since, dropping to 1-9 with Sunday’s loss. The defense has been a big part of the problem. Tennessee allowed 43 points in an overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and 40 points in a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars before Sunday’s game in Dallas. According to ESPN, the Titans are now just the fourth team since the 1970 merger to allow 40 or more points in three consecutive games, joining the 1975 Cleveland Browns, the 1981 Baltimore Colts, and the 2004 Titans. ‘Disgusting football’ On Sunday, the Cowboys racked up 480 yards of total offense. Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards, and CeeDee Lamb had 132 receiving yards. Dallas scored on every drive except the last one, when it simply kneeled out the clock. It was a disastrous performance from the Titans, and when Saleh was asked what needs to change on defense after the loss, he gave a blunt answer. “There’s a lot of things that need to change. Obviously, it’s disgusting football. It’s embarrassing football. And obviously, that starts with me,” Saleh said, via the Titans . Saleh was then asked how he can call a game when nothing is working. “That’s why I get paid. I got to figure it out,” Saleh said. He also made it clear how he wants his players to feel about the performance. “I want to — hopefully, they feel pissed. Just feeling something,” Saleh said. When asked what part of the defense needs fixing the most, Saleh pointed to his players losing their individual matchups. “When I go back and watch this tape, I have a feeling I’m going to know exactly what it is. The NFL is a game of one-on-ones, and when you get a one-on-one, you’ve got to win your opportunities. And today, they won their opportunities, and we didn’t,” Saleh said. We’ll have to see how the team bounces back from this, but it’s pretty clear that Saleh was not impressed by the showing. sports.title: Eastleigh for sale as Donald makes emotional statement
sports.description: Stewart Donald was previously owner at Sunderland [Getty Images] Eastleigh owner Stewart Donald has revealed that he will leave the club at the end of the current season after recent personal tragedy alongside the rising costs of being in the National League. He first acquired the Spitfires15 years ago, stepping away for a brief spell when he joined Sunderland before returning to the Hampshire club in April 2023. Donald led a consortium which took over the Black Cats from Ellis Short in May 2018 before selling a controlling stake in 2021. He then reinvested further funds into Eastleigh during his second spell before announcing on Sunday that he would leave the Silverlake Stadium following a turbulent and tragic period in his personal life. "Before departing [for Sunderland] I ensured the club was financially stable by leaving over three million in the club's account," Donald said in an open letter. "Upon my return these funds had understandably been exhausted and it was a difficult time for the club, including me and in hindsight I perhaps should not have returned. "But I did not want the club to be relegated and the ground needed significant work so I invested a further £1m so the club could continue at the same level. "Around that time my wife was diagnosed with cancer at 36, we had a young family. My mother sadly passed away shortly before my wife, and my father was also diagnosed with terminal cancer. "I had to spend less time at the club than I hoped, despite this my commitment never waned and I continued to fully fund the club through this period." Eastleigh sit 16th in the National League, having played in the fifth tier since winning promotion in 2014. The club parted company with manager Matt Gray in mid-November and are yet to announce a new head coach, with former boss Richard Hill conducting post-match interviews after their 3-1 win over Tamworth on Saturday. Donald shared in his letter he was actively looking for a new buyer at the club, but was yet to receive any offers from serious candidates. "At the start of the season I made the decision that it would be my last," he added. "Sadly at the moment there have been no serious candidates. There have been many enquiries but they have no credentials or serious funds. "Eastleigh currently use all of its revenues to cover the ever increasing operational costs so any investor must be prepared to fund the entire first-team budget, as I currently do. "With around five months of the season remaining, the board will seek a meeting with the supporters group to discuss the future of the club in more detail." Sunday's triumph at Estadio Coliseum was the Argentine's 345th La Liga win in his 567th match, surpassing the record for the most victories in the Spanish top flight. Simeone beat the mark of legendary former Atletico and Spain manager Luis Aragones, who won 344 matches but needed 189 more games to reach that total. "It makes me happy," Simeone said of setting the new mark, with his side now third in the table after 10 wins from 13 games. "I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this." Questioned about the perception that his team are defensive, Simeone said that was a "constant criticism we face". He added: "I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it. The 56-year-old has been in charge of Atletico since December 2011, joining the club in an era when Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid and Pep Guardiola's Barcelona were the dominant teams in Spain. He outlasted the pair of managerial superstars, leading Atletico into a period of consistent success and staying with his side long enough to witness Mourinho's return to Real this summer, 13 years after his initial departure. However he has been unable to win European football's premier competition, losing in the final to city rivals Real twice in heart-breaking fashion - in extra-time in 2014 after Real scored a stoppage-time equaliser, and on penalties in 2016. technology.description: Xfce's next release is taking shape for 2027, while MATE users have fresh options for moving their familiar desktop onto Wayland. One of the oldest surviving Linux desktops has a relatively slow release schedule: new stable releases of Xfce tend to appear every two years. The project just updated its release engineering roadmap for the forthcoming Xfce 4.22, and it looks like the next version won't arrive until early next year. We covered the release of Xfce 4.20 in December 2024, but 4.22 is still incubating. The roadmap schedules its first prerelease and feature freeze for December 15, 2026, followed by a second prerelease on January 15, 2027. A third prerelease is optional, and neither that nor the final release has a date. February or March might be plausible, but that's our guess, not the project's promise. The Xfce developers tend not to rush into things. Wayland development continues in 4.22, building on the preliminary support in 4.20. The team is also working on its own compositor, xfwl4, although the roadmap doesn't promise feature parity with X11. (In Wayland terminology, the "compositor" is the combined display server and window manager.) The compositor has its own development roadmap . The name is a nod to the current Xfce X11 window manager, which is called xfwm4 . The main developer of the new xfwl4 compositor is Brian Tarricone , who has been working on other parts of Xfce since 2004. Back in July, he shared a blog post about his use of generative-AI coding assistants called LLMs and xfwl4 . He says: "So yes, I use Claude quite a bit while developing xfwl4. I don't vibe-code, ever, and I probably use the LLM to generate less code than most people do. After all, building things with code is my hobby and passion (and I'm lucky I got to do it professionally for a quarter century), and driving an LLM is kinda boring." We find this somewhat reassuring, but any really passionate anti-LLM Xfce users reading this may be glad that the release schedules of Ubuntu LTS versions and Xfce stable releases are so far out of sync – sticking with Xubuntu 26.04 means there's no immediate need to adopt the new LLM-assisted compositor. technology.description: No Access November is going well this year. Among the many organizations to adopt Outage As A Service (OAAS) were Microsoft , Apple , the FAA , and any number of European supermarkets . Even the NSA has succumbed. For us, at least, outage is word of the year. It's certainly deeply embedded in the public mind, with schoolchildren reportedly referring to the 19th century Irish famine as "the potato outage." There's no danger of an outrage outage. OAAS is synonymous with infrastructure failure, a more useful term that begins to hint at cause and cure as well as effect. In all of the latest crop, what we know is depressingly familiar. Microsoft's O365 meltdown was a cascading failure caused by a botched upgrade that took stuff offline and melted down as it tried to come back. The FAA was a migration from Jurassic hardware that wasn't end of life so much as living fossil. The Eurofridge-cum-fondue-maker was a control system so badly written it fell apart if you raised an eyebrow at it. Clearly, nobody had. Until now. These are all different classes of OAAS that have been around for decades. Security-based outages are still outages, and a packet flood is still a packet flood whether it's a botnet DDoS or finger trouble in the config dashboard. Each of them has a root cause with obvious fixes – a faulty mental model of network/server interaction, chronic underfunding, a complete supply chain with little cyber-security expertise. All these, like the poor, will be with us always. They won't fix themselves. Infrastructure that works is invisible, and invisible things are forgotten until they break. What's needed is an infrastructure that watches itself, that is designed to be adaptive and resilient, one that refuses to connect to danger and nulls out any that gets through. There have been attempts to create a ground-up architecture that is inherently risk resistant. One such is SCION (Scalability, Control, and Isolation On Next-generation networks). It redesigns routing between domains around explicit path selection, separate control and data planes, and mechanisms for trust and failure isolation. The result is a very resilient, very reliable, and very secure infrastructure that reflects the designers' tenet that you can't patch the internet into any of these things. Start from scratch or GTFO. SCION started about 15 years ago, and it works well enough to be adopted by entities like the Secure Swiss Finance Network . If the Gnomes of Zurich trust it, no higher accreditation exists. Well, it was designed by ETH Zürich. Where you won't find it is almost everywhere else. The internet is like Switzerland in the same way the Amazon rainforest is like Central Park. There are trees and sometimes it rains. It is unwise to infer anything else. technology.title: Software issues have even reached Mercury as BepiColombo probe arrives in uncertain state
technology.description: Humanity’s third-ever mission to Mercury has arrived, but a last-minute “software issue” has complicated matters. The BepiColombo mission is a joint effort by the European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan’s Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). Reaching Mercury is not easy because its gravity is weak and its orbit is fast. The tiny planet’s proximity to the Sun further complicates matters, because our star’s gravity accelerates everything that falls towards it. BepiColombo’s journey has therefore seen it whiz past Earth once, Venus twice, and Mercury six times on a complicated path the two space agencies designed to slow it down sufficiently to be captured by mercurial gravity, while also keeping up with its rapid orbit. In 2024, the craft’s thrusters underperformed, leading the ESA and JAXA to re-plot the planned trajectory and reschedule its arrival at Mercury from mid-2025 to this past weekend. The ESA’s operations team sent the commands to insert BepiColombo into orbit on Friday. On Sunday the craft phoned home with news that it entered orbit. A little later, however, the ESA revealed “the thruster burn was shorter than planned following a software issue.” The spacecraft is safe, but the ESA says it is “working to understand what happened” and promised updates early this week. Readers may recall that a pair of NASA missions to Mars are also experiencing software glitches , which have in recent weeks become all-too-prevalent on Earth, too. Fingers crossed If all is well, BepiColombo will deploy two orbiters. The ESA’s craft is called the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO), which the ESA says will map the planet, assess the composition of its surface and interior, measure its magnetic field, and even gather data that scientists hope will “test Einstein's theory of General Relativity to an unprecedented level of accuracy.” JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MIO) will also investigate the planet’s magnetic field, plasma, dust, and atmosphere. Both orbiters are extraordinary feats of engineering. As JAXA explains , MIO is solar-powered but the sunlight it will receive at Mercury is around ten times as powerful as on Earth. Mercury itself is also sufficiently hot that the orbiter needs protection from heat radiated from the planet’s surface. ESA’s MPO keeps itself cool with three to four insulating blankets comprised of layered titanium, aluminum, and a ceramic fabric called Nextel. The blankets alone weigh 94kg. The two space agencies expect to start science operations in April 2027 but haven’t yet said if the two orbiters are in peak condition. JAXA, sadly, last week revealed that its Hayabusa2 probe has deteriorated to the point at which it can no longer make its planned landing on asteroid 1998 KY26. JAXA scheduled that for the year 2031, but problems with the probe’s thrusters mean the agency will instead attempt a high-speed fly-by of asteroid 2015 BM510 in 2028. technology.title: Techie turned his too-easy job interview into a trap
technology.description: Returning to work after the weekend can feel like voluntarily walking into a trap. To help readers feel a little freer, The Register therefore uses Monday mornings to serve up a new installment of " Who, Me? " It's the column in which we share your stories of mistakes, misjudgments, and occasional misanthropy. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Marshall," who told us about a job interview he endured about 20 years ago. The interview included a practical component he described as "Here's a PC, we've broken a few things in it, get it going." Marshall quickly spotted some mundane faults, such as a loose PCI card and unplugged internal cables. He felt the test was too easy. "One of the things I always checked was whether the power supply 110/230 switch was set for the UK," he told The Register . Getting the PC running earned Marshall a job offer, but he couldn't resist suggesting a tougher test. "I said to my future manager: 'Would it be a good thing to set the power supply to the wrong voltage as part of the interview test?' He said that wasn't fair." Marshall stayed in the job for two years. A couple of months after he left, his former manager sent him a short email. "Ha-ha, very funny." Marshall asked another former colleague what might have prompted that email. "It turned out somebody – I don't know if it was an interview candidate – had blown a power supply by not checking the voltage it was set to." What a coincidence! Or maybe not? "It wasn't anything to do with me," Marshall insisted. "No idea who it was." Have you held colleagues to a higher standard than the boss expected? Or left a little trap for them to trip over? In either case, click here to send email to Who, Me? We appreciate the chance to share your stories, and do so with appropriate anonymization so that contributors never step into the jaws of trouble. ®

technology.title: Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September
technology.description: Google’s Mandiant unit has claimed that the critical flaw VMware last week revealed in its vCenter product was under attack by a China-linked threat actor which knew of the bug in July and exploited it in September. VMware revealed several flaws on November 19. The big nasty is CVE-2026-123890, which allows unauthorized access to vCenter, the management console for hosts and guest VMs. According to seven researchers from Google’s threat intelligence group (formerly Mandiant), a crew it calls ARMORY CASTLE that it suspects of having links to the People’s Republic of China exploited CVE-2026-123890 by first compromising remote access appliances from BeyondTrust. Google’s analysis suggests the crew uses that toehold to establish access to other Linux appliances before moving deeper into victims’ networks. If the crew finds vCenter, it deploys a custom malware tool called “BONESAW” designed to slice into the VMware product. In the incident Google observed, BONESAW let attackers “forge authentication tokens, bypass MFA, and impersonate any user.” The gang put that access to work by conducting an inventory of the victim’s VMware setup, scooping up data describing the ESXi file system, attached disks, and mounted Virtual Machine File System volumes. ARMORY CASTLE also added an SSH public key to the root account’s authorized keys, and “conducted further reconnaissance and data theft on the ESXi filesystem using the root account.” Google also found evidence of BONESAW being used in July, on a server an unidentified entity had patched against CVE-2026-59309 – another authentication bypass vulnerability in vCenter. And BONESAW was just one of five tools Google thinks ARMORY CASTLE created as part of its plan to attack vCenter. It also made webshells named SLIMSAVAGE and CAGEMATCH, a backdoor called BEARBONES, and a SAML utility called SAWSNAKE. “The use of three separate specialized sets of malware and two zero-days in the course of a single campaign indicates that there are significant resources supporting ARMORY CASTLE operations,” Google’s researchers wrote. “It also shows the extent of the threat actor’s operational commitment to compromise high priority targets.” Few targets are as juicy as vCenter, because it can literally give attackers access to thousands of virtual machines and the hosts they run on. Google hasn't said how many attacks is saw on vCenter using BONESAW. The Register asked VMware if it was aware of the September attack, if it took any measures to defend its customers at the time, and to share a timeline for disclosure and remediation of CVE-2026-123890. technology.title: $1 of GPT-5.1 tokens finds new ways around China’s Great Firewall
technology.description: Researchers have found new ways to evade China’s Great Firewall after spending just $1 worth of tokens. That result appeared last week in a paper titled “CircumVolve: Automated Discovery of Censorship Evasion Strategies Using Large Language Models” presented at the Conference on Computer and Communications Security run by the Association for Computing Machinery’s Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control. Penned by six researchers from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Colorado Boulder, and activist group the Great Firewall Report, the paper points out that finding holes in the Great Firewall is a laborious process – so just the kind of task worth handing to AI. The authors came up with a tool they call “CircumVolve” and describe as “a system for automated discovery of censorship circumvention strategies across the full network stack.” “CircumVolve combines LLM code generation with iterative feedback-driven evaluation to produce verifiable and deployable evasion techniques,” they wrote. “CircumVolve models different censorship techniques as discrete scenarios, each capturing the specific context, protocol constraints, and blocking mechanisms of real-world censors. Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hypersc

science.title: What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?
science.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure? Last of the Soviet space explorers Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June. The stakes were almost immediately raised as Phobos 2 arrived in orbit around Mars on Jan. 30, 1989 , when one of the probe's three onboard flight system processors was found to have gone offline, with another already experiencing technical issues. science.title: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’
science.description: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here." This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects. A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity . This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across. Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass . Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly. One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual. By measuring the time it took for the light to return, they demonstrated a new, more precise method for tracking satellites. Since then, satellite laser ranging (SLR) has grown more precise and more widely used. The technique now underpins many aspects of Earth observation, such as validating satellite orbits and mapping subtle changes to Earth’s surface.
